summary: Hindi OCR noise from title underline in scanned PDFs
description:
## Problem

When processing scanned Hindi PDFs through the OCR pipeline, the extracted text contains significant noise — specifically `॥॥॥॥॥॥6॥॥|॥॥॥॥॥6॥|` — at the top of the first page.

## Root Cause

The noise originates from the `document_transformer` script at [`chainlit/src/scripts/document_transformer/doc_transformer/transformer.py`](chainlit/src/scripts/document_transformer/doc_transformer/transformer.py:603), which prepends a title underline made of `=` characters:

```python
paragraphs = [title, "=" * len(title)] + paragraphs
```

For a Hindi title like `सेवा अनुबंध`, this produces 14 `=` signs. When Tesseract with `lang=hin` processes this at 150 DPI (the scan generation resolution), it interprets the `=` signs as:
- `॥` (Devanagari danda, U+0965) — vertical strokes in the `=` glyph matched to danda shapes
- `6` — partial recognition of broken glyph components
- `|` — isolated vertical bar segments

## Three-Layer Fix Strategy

### Layer 1: Source Fix (Transformer)
Remove the `=` title underline in [`chainlit/src/scripts/document_transformer/doc_transformer/transformer.py`](chainlit/src/scripts/document_transformer/doc_transformer/transformer.py:603) — replace with a Devanagari-compatible separator or blank line.

### Layer 2: OCR Configuration Tuning
Modify [`chainlit/src/tools/ocr_pdf_parser.py`](chainlit/src/tools/ocr_pdf_parser.py) to pass explicit Tesseract config for Hindi:
- `--oem 1` (LSTM-only engine, better Devanagari support)
- `--psm 6` (assume single uniform text block, suppresses border noise)
- Devanagari character whitelist (U+0900–U+097F) to eliminate hallucinated characters

### Layer 3: Preprocessing & Post-Processing
- Add CLAHE contrast enhancement to [`_preprocess`](chainlit/src/tools/ocr_pdf_parser.py:208) for better stroke visibility
- Add `_cleanup_text()` post-processing to filter lines with >70% non-Devanagari punctuation

## Affected Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| [`chainlit/src/scripts/document_transformer/doc_transformer/transformer.py`](chainlit/src/scripts/document_transformer/doc_transformer/transformer.py) | Remove `=` title underline (source fix) |
| [`chainlit/src/tools/ocr_pdf_parser.py`](chainlit/src/tools/ocr_pdf_parser.py) | Add `_get_tesseract_config()`, update `_preprocess()` with CLAHE, add `_cleanup_text()` |
| [`backend/src/services/parsers/ocr_pdf_parser.py`](backend/src/services/parsers/ocr_pdf_parser.py) | Mirror same changes |
| [`chainlit/src/tests/test_ocr_pdf_parser.py`](chainlit/src/tests/test_ocr_pdf_parser.py) | Tune Hindi WER threshold after fixes verified |

## Additional Issues

Beyond the header noise, the analysis also identified:
- **Character-level corruption**: Conjunct `को` split into `्` + `ो` (stroke-continuity failure in Devanagari shirorekha)
- **Page boundary truncation**: Text cut off mid-word at page boundaries due to DPI misalignment

See [`plans/hindi-ocr-noise-analysis.md`](plans/hindi-ocr-noise-analysis.md) for the full analysis.
